content.value_statement: Analytics events often drift from schema, PII, and registration standards. This skill guides MixPanel implementation and review for Django optimo_analytics workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides a seven-step workflow for adding MixPanel event constants, schemas, registry entries, services, exports, tests, and integrations.
Provides schema patterns for UUID strings, enum fields, timestamp conversion, and strict model configuration.
Reviews analytics changes for PII fields, raw organization IDs, distinct_id selection, and missing registration.
Defines service method patterns with keyword-only arguments, fire-and-forget exception handling, and structured logging.
Lists local validation commands for linting, type checks, Django checks, tests, and targeted analytics scans.
Produces structured review reports with severity tags, issue descriptions, and recommended fixes.
limitations: The guidance is tailored to Django4Lyfe and the optimo_analytics module structure.
It does not connect to MixPanel or validate events against a live MixPanel workspace.
It depends on project files, local tooling, and test fixtures being available.
It cannot decide business event strategy without product and analytics context.

use_cases.title: Add a New Analytics Event
use_cases.description: Create a tracked event with a constant, schema, registry entry, service helper, export, tests, and business integration.

use_cases.title: Review PII-Safe Tracking
use_cases.description: Audit analytics changes for names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, UUID typing, and approved organization fields.

use_cases.title: Standardize Event Implementation
use_cases.description: Check that analytics events follow naming, distinct_id, timestamp, cron, service, and test conventions before merge.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Basic Event
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new event.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mixpanel-analytics to add tracking when a user completes profile setup. Follow the seven-step checklist and include tests.

prompt_templates.title: Review Staged Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mixpanel-analytics review on my staged analytics changes. Focus on PII protection, schema registration, service patterns, and test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Cron Event
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced event design with background processing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mixpanel-analytics to design a background-job event. Explain whether is_cron_job is needed and how timestamps should be handled.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mixpanel-analytics review across optimo_analytics. Produce a severity-tagged report with issues, evidence, and fixes.

output_examples.input: Add tracking for survey reminder notifications.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step implementation plan covering the event name, schema fields, service helper, registry entry, export, tests, and integration point.

output_examples.input: Review staged MixPanel changes for PII.
output: Summary of PII, registration, schema, service, and test status.
Severity-tagged findings with file references and fix guidance.
Recommendations for safe distinct_id and timestamp handling.

output_examples.input: Check whether a background event should use cron tracking fields.
output_examples.output: A decision note explaining when cron fields are required, how to set event time, and which timestamp fields to validate.

best_practices: Confirm event purpose and approved analytics fields before adding schema properties.
Use UUID strings and approved organization fields, never direct personal data.
Run focused tests and review output before merging analytics changes.
anti_patterns: Adding names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, or raw personal data to event schemas.
Registering a service helper without adding schema, registry, export, and tests.
Using raw organization IDs as distinct_id instead of the documented fallback prefixes.

faq.question: Does this skill send data to MixPanel?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation and review guidance for project code that sends analytics events.

faq.question: Which projects does it fit best?
faq.answer: It fits Django4Lyfe projects that use the optimo_analytics module and its existing service patterns.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill text includes Claude Code invocation notes and compatible workflow guidance.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It is written to support Codex and includes Codex installation and invocation notes.

faq.question: Does it replace privacy review?
faq.answer: No. It helps detect common PII and schema issues, but privacy owners should review sensitive event designs.

faq.question: What files does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects constants, schemas, registry, service helpers, tests, and AGENTS guidance under optimo_analytics.
